name: Abu Simbel Temples
kingdom: New Kingdom of Egypt (The Imperial Age)
description: Twin colossal rock-cut temples carved into a sandstone mountain on the bank of the Nile in Nubia, guarded by four 20-meter seated colossi.
history: Erected by Ramesses II to commemorate his victory at the Battle of Kadesh and to honor Queen Nefertari. Relocated in an international UNESCO rescue operation in 1968 to save it from the rising waters of Lake Nasser.
construction: Carved directly into living sandstone bedrock; perfectly aligned so that twice a year the rising sun penetrates 65 meters inside to illuminate the statues in the sanctuary.
architecture: Monumental rock-cut facade featuring four giant enthroned figures of Ramesses II with the solar god Ra-Horakhty above the entrance.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site; masterpiece of ancient Egyptian astronomical engineering.
currentStatus: Standing and preserved in Aswan Governorate, Egypt.
